author: Police1987
quote:
I bought GTA 6 expecting GTA and instead got something that feels like it's missing polish, soul, and heart. The gameplay is slow, clunky, and often frustrating. Most things in this game from the radio stations to the gameplay and the design choices made here all feels very flat and lacking of that GTA spark.
For a sequel that took many years and reportedly cost billions to make, I expected far more refinement.

Framerate issues and glitches aren't even my main complaint. Those can potentially be patched out over time. 

The bigger problem is that, at its core, this doesn't feel like a GTA game. If Rockstar wanted to make a Bonnie and Clyde simulator, they should have made it a different franchise.

The combat is another major disappointment. It's in a strange place where both the player and enemies can feel like bullet sponges, yet the game still finds ways to kill you with cheap deaths. It's the worst of both worlds. Gunfights drag on longer than they should, but sometimes i didnt feel truly in control of the outcome.

Features that were talked about and shown off, such as more enterable buildings, open interiors, and beaches packed with NPCs, don't feel present in the way I expected as a player. 
The world is large, but much of it feels less interactive than I was hoping for.

What disappoints me most is that the GTA spark feels largely absent. 
The humour and satire that helped define the series are at their weakest here. The jokes rarely land, the social commentary lacks the edge that made previous entries so memorable, and much of the dialogue feels surprisingly safe and forgettable. 
Moments that should be funny often fall flat, making this feel like a huge step backwards for the series.

When I think back to Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV, and GTA V, I can immediately remember characters, quotes, radio stations, and ridiculous situations years after playing them. I don't get that feeling with GTA 6.
To be fair, the game can look incredible at times. The graphics are often stunning, and there are moments where Rockstar's technical talent is impossible to ignore. Unfortunately, great visuals can't make up for gameplay that feels hollow or a world that lacks the personality and charm that made previous GTA games special.

Overall, GTA 6 looks fantastic, but beneath the graphics I found a shallow experience that lacks the freedom, personality, humour, and fun that made the series legendary.

Pound for pound, this is the weakest entry in the entire GTA series.
